# Data Dictionary: Group 24 Sports Team Balancing

**Dataset:** `data/players_raw.csv`: 62 rows (60 unique players + 2 duplicate rows), 9 columns.
**Cleaned dataset:** `data/players_clean.csv`: 60 players after removing duplicates and imputing missing values.
**Source:** synthetic. The data was generated by `data/generate_dataset.py` (seed 24) for a fictional community basketball program. No real people are described.

## Input file columns

| Column | Type | Role | Allowed values | Description | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `player_id` | text | Reference only | Unique, e.g. `P001` | Player identifier. Used to display and join results, never clustered. | Temporary ID assigned (`NEW001`) |
| `player_name` | text | Reference only | Any text | Display name (synthetic). Not needed for analysis, so the KNIME Column Filter drops it. | ID is shown instead |
| `preferred_position` | category | Balancing input (not clustered) | `Guard`, `Forward`, `Center` (any letter case) | Position the player prefers. Used to spread positions across teams, not used for distance calculations (see note 1). | Most frequent position (`Guard`) |
| `shooting` | integer | Clustering input | 1–10 | Coach's rating of scoring ability. | Median (5.0) |
| `passing` | integer | Clustering input | 1–10 | Coach's rating of ball handling and playmaking. | Median (5.5) |
| `defense` | integer | Clustering input | 1–10 | Coach's rating of on-ball and help defense. | Median (5.0) |
| `rebounding` | integer | Clustering input | 1–10 | Coach's rating of rebounding and interior play. | Median (5.0) |
| `fitness_level` | integer | Clustering input | 1–10 | Fitness rating from a standard conditioning test, converted to 1–10. | Median (6.5) |
| `availability_pct` | integer | Clustering input | 0–100 | Share of scheduled practices and games the player can attend this season. | Median (80.0) |

**Target label:** none. Clustering is unsupervised, so there is no column to predict.

**Validation rules (Python and Streamlit):**
- A value outside its allowed range, text in a number column, or an unknown position rejects the row.
- A row missing more than 2 of the 6 numeric inputs is rejected because there is too little information to place the player.
- Exact duplicate rows are removed. A repeated `player_id` with different values keeps the first row and rejects the rest.
- Boundary values (1, 10, 0, 100) are valid.

## Generated output columns

| Column | Where | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `was_imputed` | clean data, team assignments | `True` if any input for this player was filled in |
| `cluster` | team assignments | K-Means group number, 0-based (`C1` = 0). Groups are numbered from highest to lowest average skill. |
| `cluster_name` / `group` | team assignments, app | Archetype name, e.g. *Perimeter playmakers* (see `name_cluster` in `team_balancer.py`) |
| `overall_skill` | team assignments | Mean of the four skill ratings (1–10) |
| `assignment_margin` / `certainty` | team assignments, app | (d2 − d1) / d2, where d1 and d2 are the distances to the nearest and second-nearest centroid. Below 0.15, the player is flagged `uncertain`. |
| `team` | team assignments | Final balanced team, e.g. `Team 3` |

## Notes

1. **Why position is not a clustering input.** K-Means measures straight-line distance. A one-hot encoded position would add three 0/1 columns. After scaling, those columns would dominate the distance, and the clusters would simply become "guards", "forwards" and "centers". Position is instead used where it matters to a coach: making sure every team gets a fair spread of positions.
2. **Scaling.** All six numeric inputs are standardized with `StandardScaler` (z-score) before clustering. Without it, `availability_pct` (range 0–100) would outweigh the 1–10 ratings by about 10×.
3. **Data quality found in the raw file:** 2 exact duplicate rows, plus 5 missing cells: `fitness_level` ×2 (P008, P042), `shooting` ×1 (P034), `availability_pct` ×1 (P020) and `preferred_position` ×1 (P053). No out-of-range values.
4. **Edge-case file.** `data/test_roster_edge_cases.csv` holds 12 normal players plus 12 deliberately problematic rows (T01–T11 and one duplicate) for testing the interface.
